business_scope.primary_industry_name: Slip-Form Reinforced Concrete Silo Slipforming and Aeration Towers

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European doctrine grounded in Roman law; unitary national legislation, with regional legislative competencies in Catalonia, Basque Country, Navarre, Aragon, and Galicia)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed December 2020, pending ratification)
Spain-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force 1 July 2008)
Spain-United States Double Taxation Avoidance Treaty (1990, amended by 2013 Protocol)
Spain-Mexico Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force February 1996)
Spain-Chile Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (2003, revised protocol 2018)
Spain-Peru Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (1999, amended in 2018)
EU-Central America Association Agreement trade pillar (provisional application since 2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law 11/2021 of 9 July implementing EU Directive 2018/843/5AMLD; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May on implementing regulations; Royal Decree 100/2022 of 8 February establishing the Single Beneficial Ownership Register (Registro Único de Titularidades Reales) managed by the General Directorate of Registries and Notaries (DGRN) under the Ministry of Justice; Article 42 of Law 10/2010 and the Corporate Enterprises Act Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010; SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales y Delitos Monetarios) Circular 1/2021.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted to competent authorities, notaries, and obliged entities with a legitimate-interest gateway per the CJEU ruling of 22 November 2022, Case C-37/20, and Spanish Supreme Court Judgment No. 517/2023; full public access is not available)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Poder General Preventivo) granted by each intended shareholder to the incorporating attorney or legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Notary in the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (5 October 1961) certification by the competent origin-country authority, followed by acceptance before the Spanish Notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each shareholder and administrator together with NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) certificate or NIE application filing receipt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish Consulate in the shareholder's country of residence or the Spanish Directorate-General of Migration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Passport copy requires Hague Apostille or consular legalization; NIE certificate is issued directly by Spanish authorities and requires no further legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of criminal record (Certificado de Antecedentes Penales) for each natural person appointed as sole or joint Director (Administrador) of the SL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Criminal Record Registry of the country of origin, Ministry of Justice or equivalent competent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the origin state, followed by sworn Spanish translation by an official court-approved translator (Traductor Jurado)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and corporate authority resolution for any legal entity shareholder, evidencing continuing existence and board authorization to incorporate the Spanish SL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Registry or Chamber of Commerce of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the origin country's competent authority, with sworn Spanish translation attached to the incorporation file

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Pre-incorporation bank deposit certificate or bank reference letter evidencing the source and availability of the SL capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank of the shareholder's country of origin or the Spanish bank holding the provisional SL capital account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized as part of the incorporation deed and independently verified through the bank's Money Laundering Prevention Officer statutory intake procedure

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU CFSP autonomous sanctions lists (including EU Regulation 269/2014 and 833/2014), the Spanish Ministry of Economy and SEPBLAC counterterrorism and PEP guidance, and the OFAC SDN List as a cross-referenced banking standard. Screening must be executed through at least two independent data sources covering identity resolution, PEP flagging, adverse media, and frozen-assets alerts, with re-screening every 30 days and on any corporate or beneficial ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) denominación social certification platform at www.rmc.es and the Registradores de España portal at www.registradores.org
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be expressed in Spanish (Castilian) or in a co-official Spanish language (Catalan/Valencian, Basque, or Galician) where a linguistic link exists, using Latin-script characters only. Foreign ideographic or non-Latin scripts must be transliterated through an official sworn translation into a phonetically equivalent Spanish rendering before submission. The applicant must file three alternative names in order of preference in a single RMC application, and the certificate is issued based on exact-match, phonetic-similarity and misleading-similarity review under Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 (Articles 401 to 404) and Royal Decree 421/1985.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: ESPAÑA, NACIONAL, GOBIERNO, MINISTERIO (prior ministerial authorization from the Council of Ministers required)
BANCO DE ESPAÑA, INSTITUTO NACIONAL, FONDO DE GARANTÍA (prior Bank of Spain or Ministry authorization required)
MUNICIPIO, AYUNTAMIENTO, UNIVERSIDAD, COLEGIO PROFESIONAL (requires demonstrable public or institutional nexus)
SOCIEDAD ANÓNIMA, S.A., ANÓNIMA, COMANDITARIA (misleading corporate form tokens)
EXTINTA, LIQUIDACIÓN, CONCURSAL (implying dissolution, liquidation, or insolvency)
TEMPORAL, DE ACCIONES (implying a corporate form other than the intended SL)
EXTRANJERO, DEPORTIVA, JURÍDICA (potentially misleading as to nationality or activity)
OFICIAL, ESTATAL, FEDERAL, PÚBLICO (false attribution of official status)
SANTA, REY, REINA, PRÍNCIPE, CORONA (royal, papal, or religious allusions)
TERRORISMO, DROGA, VIOLENCIA, GENOCIDIO or any denomination contrary to law, public morality, or social order
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or notary may resubmit alternative names on the same working day using the RMC expedited online queue. If the rejected name is challenged by the applicant as factually or legally erroneous, a written administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) must be filed with the General Subdirectorate of Legislation and Regulation of Corporations and Securities within the Ministry of Justice within one month of notification, accompanied by the RMC negative certificate and a €20 administrative fee. The Ministry of Justice must resolve within three months; an unsatisfied applicant may then file a judicial review claim (recurso contencioso-administrativo) before the Superior Court of Justice of Madrid. Alternatively, the applicant may request a one-time extension of the valid negative certificate for an additional 90 days under Article 412 of the Commercial Registry Regulation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be accepted as the provisional registered and tax domicile for a maximum of three months post-incorporation, provided the SL holds an annual lease agreement for at least €6,000 in office sub-services within Spanish territory and at least one director is resident in the European Union. However, for the ISIC 4100 slip-form reinforced concrete silo and aeration tower EPC scope, the AEAT (Spanish Tax Agency) and SEPBLAC require demonstrable commercial substance: a physical or otherwise fully accessible office where contracts, payroll records, construction logs, and corporate books are maintained, and where the operative project-management equipment can be examined. A pure virtual mailbox without such accessibility will be presumptively treated as a shell company (sociedad pantalla) under Article 42 of Law 10/2010 and may trigger immediate company-registry and tax-audit intervention.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 12% to 18% probability of an unannounced SEPBLAC, Mercantile Registry, or AEAT physical inspection within the first three fiscal years for a newly incorporated low-risk EPC contractor using milestone wire and letter-of-credit payment rails. The risk rises to approximately 35% if the registered office depends on an opaque co-working sublease, while a dedicated construction-business physical office with a local accounting service reduces the probability to below 8%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance application fee (certificación negativa de denominación social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed tariff of approximately €10.50 per requested certification pursuant to BORME fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary fee for execution of the SL incorporation deed (escritura de constitución), including UBO declaration annex and registration presentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Public Notary (Notaría) selected by the incorporators
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff, prevailing market benchmark of €400 to €800 for a single-shareholder SL with share capital up to €3,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provincial Mercantile Registry inscription fee for the incorporation deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is located
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory sliding-scale tariff under Royal Decree 1427/1989; typical range €150 to €250 for a capital base of €1 to €3,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization processing for the five-document mandatory bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Hague Apostille authority of each shareholder's country of residence and, where applicable, the Spanish Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Published per-document fees of $20 to $50 per apostille plus consular handling charges where the origin state is not a party to the Apostille Convention

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation of apostilled foreign-issued criminal record and corporate Good Standing certificates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn Expert Translator (Traductor Jurado) registered with the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of €60 to €180 per document; two documents typically required

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE (Foreigner Identification Number) application and certificate fee for the founding shareholder and the appointed director
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Consulate in the country of origin, or the Spanish immigration office upon physical arrival
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulation 557/2011 entry and stay regime; statutory fee of approximately €9.80 per applicant

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation share capital deposit certificate (certificado de depósito de capital) or provisional blocked-account bank charge
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish financial institution selected for the SL's future operational treasury
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Common account-opening and certification fee of €50 to €90, waived upon full activation of the operational account

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil) mandatory publication fee for the incorporation announcement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Agencia Estatal Boletín Oficial del Estado
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff of approximately €21.90 per entry under Law 3/1992, Article 6

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External legal advisory and Stage-1 compliance preparation fee covering UBO profiling, AML/CFT screening, document drafting, and consular coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External counsel registered with a Spanish Bar Association (ICA) and subject to Law 10/2010 as an obliged AML professional
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Engagement fixed fee of €1,900 to €2,600 based on prevailing cross-border corporate-law benchmarks for a non-regulated EPC construction vehicle with a single foreign shareholder

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency buffer for exchange-rate movements, expedited administrative surcharges, and notarial protocol variations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Reserved internally by the incorporating counsel for regulatory fee updates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Operational contingency calculated as 10% of the aggregate of all preceding line items

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), Articles 4, 19-22, 62, 67, 124-129, 210-216; Código de Comercio Articles 119-124.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central for name certification; provincial Registro Mercantil of the registered office for inscription; Spanish notary for execution of the public deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (public deed of incorporation) electronically transmitted by the notary to the Registro Mercantil and to the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 3,000 (Art. 4 LSC), fully subscribed and paid-in at subscription; cash contributions must be deposited in an escrow account opened in the notary's name at a Spanish credit institution (Art. 62 LSC) and remain blocked until registration; non-cash contributions require an independent expert valuation report (Art. 67 LSC).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company is validly constituted under the Ley de Sociedades de Capital and its Bylaws. FIRST: The incorporation deed having been granted and subscribed, the shareholders' contributions of EUR 3,000 are ratified and accepted, constituting the subscribed share capital. SECOND: The company adopts as its registered office the premises stated in the deed and designates its legal representative for tax and administrative purposes. THIRD: Mr./Ms. [Name] is appointed Sole Administrator, with powers per Bylaw Article [X], accepting office now. FOURTH: The Administration is instructed to execute the registration filing in the Registro Mercantil, obtain the NIF, publish incorporation in BORME, and complete municipal licensing. FIFTH: Minutes approved and signed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Certification (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC), online application via the official notarial and registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official name-certification form listing up to three proposed names in descending order of preference. The RMC verifies absence of conflict with existing Spanish companies and issues a negative certificate valid for three months, renewable once. The application may be signed electronically with a qualified certificate.
required_dossiers: Solicitud de certificación negativa de denominación social
Authenticated identification or power of attorney of the incorporator
List of three proposed corporate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, file an amended request with new alternatives, or appeal the negative decision before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Escrow Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution supervised by the Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary special account in the name of the future SL or as directed by the notary and deposit the minimum paid-up capital of EUR 3,000. Obtain a bank certificate (certificado acreditativo del desembolso) identifying the depositor, beneficiary company, amount and blocking condition. The funds remain blocked until the company is registered in the Registro Mercantil.
required_dossiers: Name certificate (certificado negativo de denominación)
NIE or passport of each subscribing shareholder
Bank account application and source-of-funds declaration
Wire transfer or cash deposit confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced due diligence, supply additional notarized identification and a UBO declaration; if the account is refused, select another authorized credit institution and re-deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Grant of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the district corresponding to the proposed registered office (Colegio Notarial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators appear before the notary and execute the public deed of incorporation containing the articles of association, identities of shareholders, subscribed capital and contribution methods, registered office, and appointment of administrators. The notary verifies the name certificate, capital deposit certificate, and legal capacity, and then submits the deed electronically for registration.
required_dossiers: Valid certificate of company name
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Draft deed and draft bylaws (estatutos sociales)
NIE or passports of all subscribing shareholders
Acceptance declarations of administrators and tax identification forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any defect detected by the notary is cured by executing a supplementary or rectified deed (escritura complementaria) before the same notary within the applicable statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of ITPAJD (Actos Jurídicos Documentados) and Application for Provisional NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and the Consejería de Hacienda of the relevant autonomous community
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 business days of the deed, file the first copy of the public deed at the competent tax office and pay the Documented Legal Acts tax using Model 600. Simultaneously submit Form 036 to obtain the provisional NIF; this provisional identifier is valid until final registration and is required for subsequent registry filings.
required_dossiers: First copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
Model 600 self-assessment tax return
Model 036 census declaration
NIE or passports of incorporators and deed extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax filing is queried, submit a complementary Model 600 with late-payment interest and surcharge, or execute a rectifying deed before the notary within the special four-month assessment period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the incorporation deed to the registrar, who performs full legal qualification (calificación registral). The filing must be presented within one month of the deed date. On positive qualification, the SL acquires legal personality; the registrar issues a certificate of inscription.
required_dossiers: Electronic copy of the public deed transmitted by the notary
Proof of ITPAJD payment (Model 600)
Provisional NIF certificate
UBO declaration and any regulatory or AML screening forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar suspends or refuses registration, file a reconsideration request (recurso gubernativo) with the same registrar, then appeal to the DGSJFP, or execute a supplementary notarial deed curing the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: BORME Publication, Definitive NIF and Operational Start-up
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, the registry publishes the constitution details in the BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil). The company then obtains its definitive NIF from AEAT, completes census formalities, and may open the company current account using the registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration (inscripción registral)
BORME publication excerpt
Definitive NIF certificate
Company current account opening documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, request a certification from the registrar or submit a written admonition to the RMC; administrative silence may be cured by repeated written requests and, if necessary, judicial review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Industria of the autonomous community; municipal Ayuntamiento for activity licensing; Registro Oficial de Licitadores y Empresas Clasificadas del Sector Público for construction contractor classification.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de actividad / Declaración responsable de establecimiento industrial (apertura y funcionamiento) and, where undertaking public works, clasificación empresarial as a construction contractor.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) / autonomous community environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Screening under Anexo II of Ley 21/2013 (evaluación de impacto ambiental simplificada) where the grain silo or elevator project meets capacity thresholds; otherwise municipal environmental license or exemption upon negative environmental decision.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge limits per Real Decreto 817/2015 (including BOD5 below 40 mg/L for discharges to continental water); VOC controls per Real Decreto 117/2003; dust mitigation and air quality compliance per Ley 34/2007; waste handling per Ley 7/2022 for non-hazardous grain dust and construction waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate per Código Técnico de la Edificación (CTE DB-SI) and Real Decreto 513/2017 (RIPCI); structural load inspection per Código Estructural (Real Decreto 470/2021); workplace health and safety plan per Ley 31/1995 and Real Decreto 1627/1997, including the site-specific Plan de Seguridad y Salud for silo elevation works.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); official portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the public deed of incorporation must be presented at the relevant Registro Mercantil and, simultaneously, the provisional NIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal) is obtained from AEAT. After full registration of the company, AEAT issues the definitive NIF. For foreign entities without a permanent establishment, a non-resident NIF must be requested through a fiscal representative or by directly filing Form 036, attaching the certificate of incorporation, proof of registered office, and articles of association; the representative must be resident in Spain. The SL, as a resident entity, is subject to the general corporate income tax regime and must complete Form 036/037 for registration in the Census of Entrepreneurs, Professionals and Retainers before commencing activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident Spanish SLs are subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax) at the standard rate of 25% on worldwide income, unless the reduced 15% rate for newly created companies applies. Territorial scope is worldwide for resident entities. No general tax-exempt zone applies to the SL itself.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not implement a check-the-box system; an SL is a mandatory corporate tax resident and cannot elect pass-through treatment. Available elections include (i) the regulated group consolidation regime for groups (articles 42 et seq. of Law 27/2014), (ii) the optional reduced corporate income tax rate and certain deductions for investment, (iii) the option to apply the Special Tax Regime for ventures (start-ups) under Law 28/2022, and (iv) the applicability of the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive hybrid mismatch rules, which do not allow elective recharacterization but mandate self-correcting adjustments. VAT group status (régimen especial de grupo de entidades) may be elected under Article 163 quinquies of Law 37/1992 when economic, financial, and organizational links exist.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), the Spanish value added tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general EUR turnover threshold triggers mandatory IVA registration; every entrepreneur or professional carrying out taxable supplies in Spanish territory must apply for registration before starting activities (Ley 37/1992). For the special simplified regime (régimen simplificado), quantitative limits apply: generally EUR 250,000 per year for most agricultural and construction activities, and EUR 150,000 for certain others; crossing these limits mandates exit from the simplified regime rather than entry into the standard regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All B2B invoices must be issued electronically and transmitted in an interoperable structured format under the Crea y Crece framework (Law 18/2022), with mandatory implementation for sellers with turnover over EUR 8 million by May 2026 and all others by May 2027. In addition, large enterprises and VAT groups (under the Suministro Inmediato de Información del IVA, SII) must send invoice records to AEAT within four business days of issuance using approved web services or EDI/API. The new Verifactura system requires an electronic invoice with a digital signature or QR code verifying authenticity and integrity, and AEAT will maintain a clearing platform; non-compliant invoices are not considered legally receivable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods to destinations outside the European Union qualifies for 0% VAT under Article 21 of Law 37/1992, provided the exporter is established in Spanish territory and the goods depart from the EU within the legally required period (normally 90 days from dispatch, extendable). The zero rate applies upon proof of physical departure from the EU customs territory, obtained through the Single Administrative Document (DUA). For services relating to real property or goods exported outside the EU, or certain transportation ancillary services, the zero rate applies if the recipient is a non-established taxable person and the effective use and exploitation occurs outside the EU. Services directly connected with goods to be exported may be zero-rated with a retention of evidence of the customs export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading (maritime) or Airway Bill (air) or CMR (road transport)
Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Currency Credit Advice evidencing the receipt of payment from the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may retrospectively review export zero-rating claims within the four-year limitation period. If the required customs and payment documentation is missing or inconsistent, AEAT will assess the unpaid VAT at 21% on the presumed taxable value, plus default interest, and apply penalties under Article 27 of Law 58/2003 (late payment surcharge) and Article 191 (non-declared tax) ranging from 50% to 150% of the tax omitted. In aggravated tax fraud cases, criminal liability may arise if the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000, with penalties up to six years imprisonment. The clawback also extends to fraudulent claims made through shell structures or unrepatriated foreign currency where the exporter fails to demonstrate the real commercial transaction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem and the European Central Bank (ECB) Single Supervisory Mechanism; exchange and capital-movement statistical competence also lies with the Directorate General for International Trade and Investment (Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones) of the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies no exchange-control licensing regime; capital and current-account convertibility are fully liberalized under Articles 63-66 TFEU and Law 18/1992, with the euro as legal tender. Profit remittance obstacles are procedural only: obtain the foreign shareholder's NIE, settle the 19% non-resident income-tax withholding (reduced under applicable double-tax treaties), and file the Banco de España Balance-of-Payments statistical declaration for any cross-border payment above €10,000. Law 19/2023 on foreign direct investment additionally requires prior authorization for non-EU/EFTA investments in critical infrastructure, defence, dual-use technology or national-security areas; an ISIC 4100 grain-silo-elevator EPC business is not presumptively within those sectors, provided no site lies near a regulated military or state-security perimeter.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement in Spain: no conversion ratio, no deposit timeline and no repatriation quota are imposed by the Banco de España or the Eurosystem. An exporting SL may retain foreign-currency receipts indefinitely in multi-currency accounts and convert at commercial market rates. The sole compliance layer is statistical and fiscal: cross-border transactions exceeding €10,000 must be reported through the Banco de España BOPS electronic declarations, and export gains must be recognized for Corporate Income Tax (IS) purposes at the ECB reference exchange rate on accrual, with supporting SWIFT/LC evidence retained for six years under Law 10/2010 AML rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account plus multi-currency Operational Account; trade finance desk for MT700 issuance
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account; FX forward and LC workflows under one digital signature
Operational Account with milestone earmarking for construction payments and SEPA vendor sweeps
Operational Account / Import LC facility for silo slip-form equipment from third-country manufacturers
Operational Account and cash-pooling host; limited trade-product depth for agricultural EPC
Regional Operational Account; viable only when the silo project sits within Castilla y León or Andalucía core networks

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium feasibility: only European Economic Area (EEA) Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) validly passported into Spain under Law 21/2011 and PSD2 may lawfully serve as payment-account or e-money processors; they can expedite SEPA concentration and supplier disbursements but are not acceptors of statutory share-capital deposits because Spanish Notaries require a deposit certificate from a credit institution (bank) to authenticate the capital desembolso. Offshore, non-EEA EMIs have no legal mandate in Spain, cannot provide the notarial escrow evidence, and their use as treasury rail exposes the SL to adverse AML classification under Law 10/2010; therefore they should be confined to ancillary collection gateways only after a tier-1 bank account is live.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance is the operative default: at least one duly appointed director or a Spanish-resident attorney-in-fact holding a notarized power of attorney must appear physically at the bank branch for a personal KYC interview presenting the original escritura de constitución, Registro Mercantil certificate, NIE cards and passports. Fully remote onboarding is technically possible for domestic low-risk SLs under EBA digital-identification guidance, but becomes unavailable where the ultimate beneficial owner is a foreign corporate shareholder; the bank will apply enhanced due diligence and require either a video-KYC plus apostilled corporate package or a physical branch visit, at the bank's discretion. Plan for a physical closing day in Madrid or the project province before activating escrow or operational flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder incorporated in a jurisdiction on FATF grey-listing, Spain's Royal Decree 304/2014 high-risk list, or an EU non-cooperative jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of tax residence from the foreign tax authority, audited financial statements for the prior two years, a complete natural-person UBO chain on the official Spanish UBO register form, bank reference letter from the shareholder's credit institution, and a notarized statement of the commercial rationale for owning the Spanish grain-silo EPC vehicle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing NIE for any non-resident director or missing inscription of the SL deed in the Registro Mercantil at onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: NIE certificates for each director and shareholder, certified copy of the escritura de constitución, certificate of registration and incorporation from the Registro Mercantil, plus the appointment deed of an authorized Spanish-resident administrator (with NIE) for service of process and banking operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed person (PEP) status of an ultimate shareholder, or layered offshore holding creating opacity above the Spanish SL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP screening declaration with passport copies, twelve-month bank statements evidencing the source of wealth, the official UBO register extract or notarized UBO attestation, and a sworn statement that no public funds, state-linked entities or third-party nominee accounts are used to finance the construction company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial inbound capital injection routed through multiple intermediary banks in a non-EEA corridor, triggering source-of-funds scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full SWIFT MT103 chain, the signed ISIC 4100 grain-silo-elevator construction contract or investment commitment letter, commercial registration extract of the foreign counterparty, certified translation of the project agreements, and a board resolution authorizing the exact contribution amount and account destination.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Share capital must be wired before or simultaneously with notarization into the escrowed capital account opened in the name of the SL in formation. Where the entity adopts the progressive-formation (SLFS) modality under the Ley Crea y Crece, the initial subscribed amount may be below the €3,000 default statutory floor, but every subsequent capital increase must follow the same notarial deposit-certificate protocol. Routing in EUR uses SEPA Instant/TARGET2; routing in USD or third-country currency uses SWIFT MT103, with the remittance-information field carrying the purpose code mapped to 'Direct investment – incorporation and capital increase' and the beneficiary account exactly mirroring the notarial deed. Simultaneously, the transaction must be declared to the Banco de España BOPS portal and, if the foreign investor is non-EU/EFTA, screened against Law 19/2023 prior-authorization triggers. The Notary issues the deposit certificate only upon receipt of the bank's verifiable confirmation, after which the Registro Mercantil inscription proceeds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic disbursements run over SEPA Credit Transfer (IBAN-based, same-day via TARGET2) and, for recurring subcontractor and material bills, SEPA Direct Debit. Cross-border trade settlements to non-EEA equipment vendors (slip-form rails, aeration towers, grain-handling steel) are executed by SWIFT MT103 against proof-of-shipment documents, or through irrevocable commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) advised via SWIFT MT700 and paid by MT103/MT202 upon presentation of compliant documents (commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, inspection certificate). Performance and advance-payment risks to the EPC client are covered by standby letters of credit (ISP98) or bank guarantees (U-form) issued by the onboarding tier-1 bank against the project's escrow and milestone milestones, preserving the low-risk AML classification of the construction flows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable outright forwards traded bilaterally with the onboarding tier-1 bank under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and a Credit Support Annex.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in EUR/BRL, EUR/MXN and other Latin American currencies to hedge expected USD- or local-currency receipts from export bridge contracts.
Cross-currency swaps fixed-floating and fixed-fixed, permitted for longer-dated EUR/USD or EUR/other exposure arising from shareholder subordinated loans and capex financing.
Vanilla FX options, collars and zero-premium structures under MiFID II suitability rules, approved through the entity's EII (professional client) classification.

Spot-FX forwards and short-term FX swaps for working-capital roll-over of import LCs; all OTC derivative contracts are subject to EMIR reporting, bilateral margin where thresholds are exceeded, and intra-group hedging documentation where the parent treasury centralizes risk.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate under Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law. Newly incorporated companies may generally apply a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory exclusions and anti-abuse conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taxable profit is determined from accounting profit with statutory adjustments. Available incentives may include deductions for qualifying research and development and technological innovation, employment-related incentives, donations, double-tax relief, and regional incentives in the Canary Islands, Basque Country, or Navarre where applicable. Qualifying small entities may apply statutory accelerated depreciation and other SME incentives. The general minimum taxation rules and limits on tax credits may restrict the effective benefit. Spain has no general tax holiday for ordinary mainland construction activities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited; Spanish tax losses generally have no statutory expiry period. Annual utilization is subject to percentage limitations based on the taxpayer's prior-year net turnover, with a generally available minimum offset of EUR 1 million and additional restrictions for ownership changes or special cases.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax and Non-Resident Income Tax return for entities with a permanent establishment, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic headquarters using an authorized electronic certificate or equivalent approved authentication.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is generally due within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. Electronic filing deadlines may be extended to the next business day where legally applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SL's legal name, Spanish tax identification number, registered office, tax period dates, legal form, activity classification, group status, and filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder must not be reported as the taxpayer unless the activity is carried on through a Spanish permanent establishment or a Spanish resident subsidiary. The Spanish SL files as a resident entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the accounting result for the tax period based on statutory financial statements before corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SL's Spanish statutory accounts. Transactions with non-resident owners, contractors, lenders, or group companies must be separately supported by contracts and accounting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add or deduct permanent and temporary differences, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation adjustments, impairment, interest limitation, related-party adjustments, exempt income, and prior-year tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish deductibility rules rather than the shareholder's home-country accounting or tax treatment. Cross-border payments require withholding, beneficial-owner, arm's-length, and treaty documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter available tax losses, utilization during the period, remaining balance, and any limitation calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain evidence of losses, filed returns, accounting records, and continuity of ownership. Ownership changes may restrict losses where statutory anti-trafficking conditions are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax base and gross tax liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the positive taxable base and apply the applicable rate, including the general 25% rate or a qualifying 15% rate for newly incorporated entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 15% start-up rate is not automatically available to every new company and requires review of prior activity, related entities, ownership, and asset-holding status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim double-tax relief, research and development or technological innovation credits, donations, employment incentives, and other legally available deductions, subject to evidence and statutory caps.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits require proof of foreign tax paid and compliance with limitation rules. Treaty relief does not replace Spanish return filing or record-retention obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit Spanish withholding tax, payments on account, and Modelo 202 installment payments against the final liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend, interest, royalty, service, or lease payments to non-residents must be reconciled with Modelo 216 and Modelo 296 withholding reporting where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the amount payable or refundable and select direct debit, electronic payment, or refund instructions through AEAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made by the filing deadline. A refund claim should be supported by reconciliations, bank details, and evidence supporting all credits and deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report corporate income tax payments on account, generally due in the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December, subject to the applicable calculation method and statutory exceptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Spanish SL is ordinarily within the installment regime unless an exemption or zero-liability condition applies. Large companies may be subject to the minimum installment payment rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without tax payable may trigger a fixed penalty generally starting at EUR 200, ordinarily reducible for voluntary compliance. Late filing with tax payable generally triggers a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus late-payment interest. Incorrect or incomplete returns may attract penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on severity, concealment, or fraud. Late payment may generate interest, enforcement surcharges, asset attachment, and collection proceedings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 216, withholding and payment on account for income obtained by non-residents without a permanent establishment, and Modelo 296, annual information return, filed electronically through AEAT.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Modelo 216 generally monthly for large withholders and quarterly for other withholders; Modelo 296 annually
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 216 is generally due within the first 20 calendar days of the month following the relevant month or quarter. Modelo 296 is generally due during the first 20 calendar days of January following the reporting year, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Spanish SL's tax identification number, legal name, address, reporting period, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the Spanish SL as withholding agent even where the recipient is a foreign parent, contractor, lender, or licensor.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the recipient's name, foreign tax identification number, country of residence, beneficial-owner information where required, and income category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Collect a current tax residence certificate before applying treaty relief. A payment to an intermediary does not establish treaty entitlement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Gross income, exemption, rate, and tax withheld
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross payment, statutory or treaty exemption, applied rate, and tax withheld for dividends, interest, royalties, services, leases, or other Spanish-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not apply a reduced treaty rate solely on the basis of the recipient's incorporation jurisdiction. Verify residence, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse requirements, and any EU directive conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile all periodic withholding filings by recipient, payment type, gross amount, exemption, and tax withheld.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amounts reported in Modelo 296 must reconcile to the general ledger, bank records, contracts, invoices, and periodic Modelo 216 filings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold or remit may result in assessment of the tax not withheld, late-payment interest, and penalties generally linked to the underpaid amount. Filing, data, or reporting failures may generate fixed penalties, with higher penalties for concealment, repeated non-compliance, or fraudulent arrangements.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. A qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply to a corporate EU or qualifying EEA parent generally holding at least 10% for the required continuous period, subject to taxation, anti-abuse, and beneficial-ownership conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain a valid tax residence certificate from the recipient's tax authority before payment, confirm treaty residence and beneficial ownership, analyze the relevant treaty article, ownership and holding-period tests, anti-abuse provisions, and any principal-purpose or domestic anti-avoidance rule, then apply the treaty rate at source where permitted. Retain the certificate, corporate ownership chart, board resolutions, contracts, payment records, and substance evidence. If excess withholding was imposed, the recipient may generally seek a refund from AEAT using the prescribed non-resident refund procedure. Treaty relief does not eliminate Modelo 216 and Modelo 296 obligations where reporting is required.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Spanish non-resident withholding is generally 24% for non-residents outside the EU and EEA and 19% for residents of the EU or qualifying EEA jurisdictions, subject to statutory conditions. Interest and royalties may qualify for a treaty-reduced rate. Qualifying associated-company payments of interest and royalties within the EU may be exempt under the Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, generally requiring qualifying legal forms, minimum 25% direct ownership or equivalent group relationship, a minimum holding period, subject-to-tax status, and beneficial ownership. Payments to related parties must also satisfy Spanish transfer-pricing and anti-abuse rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 aggregate annual transaction value with the same related person, calculated at arm's-length value, is the principal threshold below which the detailed local documentation exemption may apply for transactions of the same type and under the same valuation method. The exemption generally does not cover certain real estate, intangible-asset, or tax-haven transactions. A Spanish entity belonging to a multinational group may require a Master File, and groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million may require Country-by-Country reporting. There is no single universal Master File threshold applicable to every group.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent valuation methods where the listed methods are not reliable or appropriate
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations filing regime. Nevertheless, Spanish anti-abuse rules, the beneficial-ownership requirement, the principal-purpose test, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, hybrid mismatch rules, general anti-avoidance provisions, and EU anti-abuse standards require genuine commercial substance. The SL should maintain Spanish management and decision-making evidence, qualified personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or operational infrastructure appropriate to its construction activity, project records, risk control, financing rationale, and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of revenue, false invoices, concealed cash receipts, fabricated construction costs, improper deduction of private expenses, or intentional understatement of corporate income tax, VAT, or withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, together with tax assessment, interest, and collection measures. Tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax and tax period may constitute a criminal offense, generally punishable by imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of 1 to 6 times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and higher fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or de facto managers who participate in, authorize, or negligently facilitate the conduct may face criminal liability, civil restitution, personal administrative liability in qualifying cases, disqualification from public office or management, and asset-securing measures. Travel restrictions are not automatic and require statutory or judicial grounds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoicing and VAT carousel arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or accepting invoices for nonexistent silo construction, engineering, subcontracting, transport, or materials, deducting unsupported input VAT, or using interposed entities to circulate invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of improperly claimed VAT and corporate deductions, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties commonly calculated by reference to the unpaid or unduly refunded tax. Serious or organized fraud may trigger criminal tax, commercial-document, or accounting offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who knowingly approve or use fictitious invoices may incur criminal and civil liability. Directors may be liable for losses caused by breach of diligence duties and may face asset measures, disqualification, or imprisonment where the conduct satisfies a criminal offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length management fees, shareholder loans, guarantees, engineering charges, procurement margins, or asset transfers; missing Local File or Master File; or unsupported allocation of project profits to foreign affiliates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may make a primary adjustment and corresponding adjustments, assess tax and interest, and impose documentation-related penalties. Specific documentation penalties may apply per omitted, inaccurate, or incomplete data, subject to statutory caps; broader tax underpayment penalties may apply where tax is concealed or fraudulently avoided.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for approving materially unsupported related-party arrangements. Criminal exposure normally requires additional fraudulent conduct meeting the statutory elements of a tax, accounting, or commercial offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper treaty or EU directive relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying zero or reduced withholding without a valid residence certificate, paying a conduit entity, misrepresenting beneficial ownership, artificially satisfying holding requirements, or routing payments through a shell company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SL may be assessed for withholding tax, interest, and penalties. Anti-abuse rules may deny treaty or directive relief and recharacterize the payment or arrangement according to its economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly provide false information or approve abusive withholding positions may face civil liability, administrative sanctions, and criminal liability where fraud, document falsification, or tax evasion thresholds are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SL solely as an invoicing, financing, dividend-routing, or profit-shifting vehicle without personnel, decision-making, project control, commercial risk, or credible business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may apply recharacterization, conflict-in-application or simulation doctrines, deny deductions and treaty benefits, assess tax and interest, and impose penalties where applicable. Related-party payments may be reclassified as dividends or hidden profit distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability and, in abusive or fraudulent cases, criminal liability. Corporate separateness is not automatically disregarded; veil piercing generally requires abuse of legal personality, fraud, insolvency abuse, or unlawful harm to creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold tax from non-resident recipients, employees, directors, or contractors; misclassification of employees as independent subcontractors; or failure to remit payroll taxes and social-security contributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company may owe unpaid withholding, payroll tax, social-security contributions, interest, surcharges, and administrative penalties. Serious labor or social-security fraud may trigger criminal liability, particularly where workers' rights or public funds are materially affected.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly or subsidiarily liable in legally defined circumstances, particularly following non-compliance, insolvency, or failure to take corrective action. Criminal liability may include fines or imprisonment depending on the offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash, payments from unrelated third parties, opaque beneficial owners, sanctioned persons, circular letters of credit, or project funds inconsistent with the customer's profile; failure to perform required customer due diligence or report suspicious activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious breaches may lead to public or private reprimands, fines that can reach the higher of statutory fixed amounts, EUR 10 million, or 10% of annual total turnover for certain very serious breaches, together with management disqualification in applicable cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and officers responsible for AML failures may face personal administrative sanctions, civil liability, and criminal liability for money laundering or terrorist-financing participation. Travel bans are not automatic and require a competent-authority or judicial measure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Construction-sector licensing, safety, and subcontracting violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Performing regulated engineering or construction work without required professional authorizations, falsifying safety records, using undeclared labor, ignoring occupational-health requirements, or breaching subcontracting-chain controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Labor, occupational-safety, construction, and sector regulators may impose fines, work stoppages, loss of eligibility for public contracts, contractor disqualification, and civil liability for accidents. Fatal or serious workplace incidents may result in criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and site managers may face civil restitution, administrative sanctions, professional disqualification, and imprisonment for deliberate or grossly negligent conduct causing injury, death, or serious worker-rights violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining double books, destroying project records, concealing liabilities, distributing dividends from unlawful profits, preferring related creditors, or continuing to trade while materially insolvent without appropriate action.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include rejection of accounts, tax reassessment, director liability for insolvency deficits, clawback of unlawful distributions, creditor claims, insolvency disqualification, and criminal penalties for accounting or insolvency offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to restore assets, compensate creditors, return unlawful distributions, or cover all or part of the insolvency shortfall. Imprisonment is possible where the conduct constitutes a criminal offense; travel restrictions require judicial authorization and are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Supplying silo equipment, engineering services, financing, or technical assistance to sanctioned persons, embargoed jurisdictions, or prohibited end users through a disguised intermediary or false trade documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transactions may be blocked or confiscated and may attract administrative fines, loss of licenses, contracting restrictions, and criminal penalties under applicable Spanish, European Union, and international sanctions regimes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who knowingly authorize prohibited transactions may face personal civil, administrative, and criminal liability. Asset freezes, investigative measures, and judicial travel restrictions may apply where legally ordered.
